blocks.text: 华为是中国最大的 AI 芯片开发商，它正依托中国充沛的能源建设数据中心。然而，受美国出口管制影响，它在芯片性能和能效上都落后于美国竞争对手英伟达。

blocks.text: 以华为位于内蒙古和林格尔的 AI 数据中心为例，按 AI 算力规模计算，它是中国最大的数据中心之一，但容量不到全球最大的 AI 数据中心——田纳西州的 Colossus 2——的十分之一。从未来的建设规划看，至少到 2028 年，它仍将远远落后于 Colossus。

blocks.text: 本文借助卫星图像和公开资料，考察和林格尔园区以及华为更广泛的 AI 基础设施计划，说明我们是如何得出上述结论的。

inlines.text: 本文借助卫星图像和公开资料，考察和林格尔园区以及华为更广泛的 AI 基础设施计划，说明我们是如何得出上述结论的。

blocks.text: 和林格尔园区：AI 用 IT 电力容量最高可达 286 兆瓦

inlines.text: 和林格尔园区：AI 用 IT 电力容量最高可达 286 兆瓦

blocks.text: 华为和林格尔园区位于和林格尔新区，由西、南、北三个区域组成。卫星图像显示，当地村庄已被拆除，为数据中心腾出土地。

inlines.text: 华为和林格尔园区位于和林格尔新区，由西、南、北三个区域组成。卫星图像显示，当地村庄已被拆除，为数据中心腾出土地。

blocks.text: 该园区很可能服务多种终端用户和应用，但华为的文件显示，园区配备的是主要面向大模型训练和推理的“超节点”服务器，这意味着园区很大一部分是专门用于 AI 的。

inlines.text: 该园区很可能服务多种终端用户和应用，但华为的文件显示，园区配备的是主要面向大模型训练和推理的“超节点”服务器，这意味着园区很大一部分是专门用于 AI 的。

blocks.text: 我们购买了这些区域的商业高分辨率卫星图像，用来估算建筑的电力容量。主要方法是冷却设备模型：根据可见冷却机组的类型、尺寸和数量，估算其排热能力，进而推算建筑的 IT 电力容量。

inlines.text: 我们购买了这些区域的商业高分辨率卫星图像，用来估算建筑的电力容量。主要方法是冷却设备模型：根据可见冷却机组的类型、尺寸和数量，估算其排热能力，进而推算建筑的 IT 电力容量。

blocks.text: 卫星图像显示，每个区域都包含几乎相同的三层建筑。但北区的冷却塔数量远少于西区和南区，说明北区的建筑不太可能容纳高性能 AI 芯片——现代 AI 服务器的功率密度往往是行业平均水平的 10 倍以上。

blocks.text: 排除低密度的北区后，剩下四栋看起来已经完工、冷却设施密集的建筑：南区和西区各两栋。我们的冷却模型估算，这四栋建筑合计 IT 电力容量为 286 兆瓦（MW）。

blocks.text: 我们观察到若干线索，表明这些建筑已在运行。首先，从外观上看，这些建筑基本完工，包括冷却设备、备用发电机和停车场，没有仍在施工的迹象。其次，一张卫星图像显示，至少一栋建筑的蒸发冷却塔上方似乎有凝结水汽，说明该建筑正在运行。第三，在另一张图像中，多台冷却塔风扇带有彩色的“残影”，表明风扇正在转动。1

blocks.text: 数据中心的AI算力通常被划分为多个高密度互联的集群，总容量未必能合并用于训练同一个AI模型。不过，即便华为和林格尔的算力被拆分为多个集群，仍可运行大规模研发实验。仅华为和林格尔估算AI算力的10%（即8,100 H100e），就足以在一个月内训练一个DeepSeek-V4-Pro规模的模型。在最乐观的情况下，若将华为和林格尔当前全部算力合并用于单次训练，训练一个GPT-6 Astra规模的模型需要一年。

blocks.text: 如果到2028年初算力再增加70%以上，华为和林格尔的算力将达到约141,000 H100e（90%置信区间：65,000至227,000）。但即便如此，它在Colossus 2容量中所占的份额仍大致持平，甚至更小——我们预计Colossus 2到2028年至少达到180万H100e。这并不一定意味着中国数据中心的整体前沿水平会进一步落后。例如，华为位于芜湖的姊妹园区增长速度会略快一些，预计到2027年12月达到151,000 H100e。

blocks.text: 这对中国AI意味着什么

inlines.text: 这对中国AI意味着什么

blocks.text: 中国似乎拥有充足的能源来支撑数据中心。许多针对AI优化的设施正以数百兆瓦的容量建设，并搭载国产芯片。然而，美国AI数据中心每单位电力所支撑的AI算力是中国的2.5倍，其中最大的已经达到1,000 MW。华为和林格尔数据中心就是这一差距的典型例子，其算力仅为田纳西州Colossus 2的7%。正因如此，中国在过去两年能做出如此出色的AI模型就更令人印象深刻。但中国的算力约束在未来两年内不太可能缓解，这意味着其AI能力和部署规模将继续落后于美国。

inlines.text: The Huawei Horinger campus consists of three zones (West, South, and North) within the Horinger New Area. Satellite imagery shows that villages have been demolished to make way for data centers there.

blocks.text: While the campus likely serves a diverse set of end users and applications, Huawei documentation indicate it is equipped with “hypernode” servers that are primarily designed for large-model training and inference, which suggests a large portion of the campus is specialized for AI.

blocks.text: We acquired commercial high-resolution satellite images of these zones to help estimate the power capacity of the buildings. Our primary method is a cooling equipment model: based on the type, size, and number of cooling units visible, we estimate their heat rejection capacity and, in turn, the buildings’ IT power capacity.

inlines.text: We acquired commercial high-resolution satellite images of these zones to help estimate the power capacity of the buildings. Our primary method is a cooling equipment model: based on the type, size, and number of cooling units visible, we estimate their heat rejection capacity and, in turn, the buildings’ IT power capacity.

blocks.text: The satellite imagery revealed that each zone contains nearly identical three-story buildings. However, the North zone has far fewer cooling towers than the West and South zones, suggesting that its buildings are unlikely to house powerful AI chips — modern AI servers tend to be more than 10 times as power-dense as the industry average.

blocks.text: Excluding the low-density North zone, we were left with four apparently complete buildings with dense cooling infrastructure: two in the South and two in the West. Our cooling model estimates a total of 286 megawatts (MW) of IT power capacity across these four buildings.

blocks.text: We’ve observed several clues suggesting the buildings are operational. As a prerequisite, the buildings appear more or less complete from the outside, including cooling, backup generators, and carparks, with no signs of ongoing construction. Second, one satellite image shows what appears to be condensed water vapor above at least one evaporative cooling tower at one building, suggesting the building is operating. Third, multiple cooling tower fans have colored “ghosts” in another image, which indicates that the fans are moving.1

As a prerequisite, the buildings appear more or less complete from the outside, including cooling, backup generators, and carparks, with no signs of ongoing construction. Second, one satellite image shows what appears to be condensed water vapor above at least one evaporative cooling tower at one building, suggesting the building is operating. blocks.text: Only one of the four buildings, in the West zone, has yet to show any signs of operation. A public disclosure implies it was complete but not yet operational as of September 2026. We estimate it will become operational by December, while the other three are already up and running.

blocks.text: Estimating Horinger’s compute

inlines.text: Estimating Horinger’s compute

blocks.text: The physical scale of the Huawei Horinger campus is impressive, but its compute capacity is more important for assessing China’s AI capabilities.

inlines.text: The physical scale of the Huawei Horinger campus is impressive, but its compute capacity is more important for assessing China’s AI capabilities.

blocks.text: Based on estimates of when power-intensive buildings at this site became operational, we used Huawei chip sales over time to estimate the chips that would fill those racks, assuming a four-month lag from sale to deployment.This resulted in a mix of Ascend 910C and 910B chips in the first building (mostly 910C), and 100% 910C in the other three buildings. Given that one building is not operational yet, we find that about 105,000 Ascend 910C chips and 8,000 Ascend 910B chips are operational to date.

blocks.text: To compare Chinese and US chips, a common baseline is in “H100-equivalents” (H100e), comparing performance to the output of one H100 chip. Disclosures from Huawei point to the 910C performing at around 0.76 H100e. Meanwhile, Nvidia’s B200 and B300 chips perform at about 2.5 H100e.

blocks.text: We believe this estimate is plausible given what we know about total chip production and deployments at other data centers. According to the chip sales estimates, 907,000 Ascend 910C and 600,000 Ascend 910B chips had been sold by the end of March 2026. Satellite imagery indicates that the third AI building at Horinger was operational by August 2026. With a four-month lag between sale and deployment, our estimate suggests Huawei Horinger had used 11% of the total 910C stock by August.

blocks.text: Horinger has 7% as much AI compute as the global frontrunner

inlines.text: Horinger has 7% as much AI compute as the global frontrunner

blocks.text: At 81,000 H100-equivalents, Huawei Horinger is a large AI data center by today’s standards, and probably one of the largest in China. We have done a broad search of Chinese AI data centers across major hubs, and reviewed several top contenders in depth. Of those, only VNET Bayin Ulanqab and Huawei Wuhu are likely to match or slightly exceed Huawei Horinger.

blocks.text: However, Huawei Horinger is much further from the largest AI data center in the world. That title goes to SpaceX’s Colossus 2 in Tennessee. Colossus 2 has about 14 times as much computing capacity as Huawei Horinger.

inlines.text: However, Huawei Horinger is much further from the largest AI data center in the world. That title goes to SpaceX’s Colossus 2 in Tennessee. Colossus 2 has about 14 times as much computing capacity as Huawei Horinger.

blocks.text: The AI compute in a data center campus is often separated into multiple densely-networked clusters, and the total capacity cannot necessarily be combined to train one AI model. However, large R&D experiments could be run even if the compute at Huawei Horinger is split into many clusters. Just 10% of Huawei Horinger’s estimated AI compute, at 8,100 H100e, is enough to train a DeepSeek-V4-Pro scale model in one month. In a very optimistic scenario, if all of Huawei Horinger’s current compute was combined for a single training run, a model the scale of GPT-6 Astra would take one year to train.

blocks.text: Next phase: 70% more computing power by early 2028

inlines.text: Next phase: 70% more computing power by early 2028

blocks.text: The buildout at Huawei Horinger is far from complete. As discussed above, one of the four buildings has yet to become operational, and at least three new buildings are planned beyond the six already built, based on renderings and construction sites seen in satellite imagery.

inlines.text: The buildout at Huawei Horinger is far from complete. As discussed above, one of the four buildings has yet to become operational, and at least three new buildings are planned beyond the six already built, based on renderings and construction sites seen in satellite imagery.

blocks.text: One of these new buildings is already underway in the South zone, and based on the pace of construction, we expect it to be operational in February 2028. Assuming the new building is as AI-focused as the existing buildings, the campus could grow its total AI compute by over 70% by early 2028.

blocks.text: With over 70% more computing power by the start of 2028, Huawei Horinger would reach about 141,000 H100e (90% CI: 65,000 to 227,000). But this would still leave it at about the same share, or a smaller one, of Colossus 2’s capacity, which we expect to reach at least 1.8 million H100e by 2028. This does not necessarily mean the overall frontier of Chinese data centers will fall further behind. For instance, Huawei’s sister campus in Wuhu will grow slightly faster, reaching a projected 151,000 H100e by December 2027.

blocks.text: What this means for Chinese AI

inlines.text: What this means for Chinese AI

blocks.text: China appears to have abundant energy for data centers. Many AI-optimized facilities are being built with hundreds of megawatts of capacity and filled with domestically-produced chips. However, AI data centers in the US support 2.5 times more AI compute per unit of power, and the largest among them have already reached 1,000 MW. The Huawei Horinger data center is a key example of this gap, with just 7% of the computing capacity of Colossus 2 in Tennessee. This makes it even more impressive that China has produced such capable AI models in the past two years. But China’s compute constraints are unlikely to ease in the next two years, which suggests that their AI capabilities and deployment capacity will continue to lag behind those of the US.

blocks.text: The principle is that fans sometimes reflect glare into the satellite image sensor, and the sensor captures red, green, and blue wavelengths at slightly different points in time. When a fan is moving, the glare can occur precisely when only one of these wavelengths is captured, making the glare appear in one bright color.
